designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Clean, consistent icon strokes that burn and hold well in one white ink on black; tight grid, strong bold headline, and the joke reads instantly from distance. The tiny condensed labels are the weak point: around 0.15-0.2 in cap height at print size they will fill in or fuzz on a white underbase over cotton, and the whole block sits small and narrow on the back.
designs.fix: Enlarge the labels (or drop to a bolder weight with more tracking) so they hold at 230-mesh, and scale the full block up roughly 15-20% so it fills the back properly.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: Charming, airy brush drawings with confident line weight that prints cleanly in one ink on either tee; the repeated 'Turn around.' is a great comic rhythm and the serif captions are legible. Lots of open negative space keeps ink coverage light and the hand soft. Risk is small detail: thin brush tapers and the tiny moon may break up, and at the mockup scale the captions get small.
designs.fix: Thicken the thinnest brush tapers to a minimum ~1 pt at final print size and bump the caption size slightly so the steps read from a few metres.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Very well drawn, crisp line art with a universally understood gag and a clear 1-2-3 read; tabby stripes give nice solid-ink texture for one colour. Production concerns: the cat-bed fur hatching and box crease lines are hairline-thin and will drop out or plug, especially white on black; panel 2 loses the box (just a horizontal floor line), weakening continuity; and the tall stack prints narrow on the back.
designs.fix: Bring all hairlines (bed texture, box flaps, tape) up to a minimum ~1 pt stroke at print size and keep the box visible in panel 2 so the three panels read as one sequence.
